briefs.title: Sample brief: themes in the public gold headlines, 21 November 2026
briefs.summary_markdown:
This file is the schema example for research bots. It describes themes in public headlines on this date. It is not a Gold Radar forecast and not a recommendation.

On 21 November 2026 the free headline feeds were led by reports of a sharp weekly fall in the gold price. Publishers including Kitco, BullionVault, FOREX.com and Investing.com described a deep weekly decline. A separate Investing.com headline reported Goldman discussing central-bank demand, and another reported UBS discussing further weakness. Those are the publishers' words, summarised so the shape of a brief is visible.

How to read the rest of the desk: the large price is a named spot print. A sparkline that uses a different free series says so. Headline tone is a keyword count. Consensus forecast and previous on the calendar are the data vendor's figures.
bull_case: Some headlines in the feed still discussed central-bank demand as a theme commentators attach to gold. That is a description of those headlines, not a case for taking a position.
A brief lists supportive themes on this side so they can be read next to the opposing themes. Listing a theme is not a recommendation.
bear_case: Several headlines described a large weekly fall in the gold price and used words such as slump, selloff and weakness. That records the tone of the coverage.
A UBS headline in the feed discussed further weakness. That is that firm's published comment, not a Gold Radar view.
briefs.key_levels_watched_by_market_text: Some headlines used the words support and uptrend. This desk does not turn those words into prices to act on. Nothing here is an entry, an exit, a target or a stop.
